questions.stem: A 77 year old man has 6 weeks of aching and stiffness in both shoulders and hips. He struggles to comb his hair and to get out of a low chair, and the stiffness lasts about 2 hours each morning. He has lost his appetite and feels feverish. His temperature is 37.6°C.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Over 50, bilateral shoulder and hip girdle stiffness over 45 minutes, systemic upset, raised ESR/CRP and normal CK = PMR.

Raises CK and causes true weakness.
Causes true proximal weakness with a raised CK; his CK is normal.

steps.x: **C. Polymyalgia rheumatica.** Older patient + girdle stiffness + high ESR/CRP + normal CK = PMR.

questions.e: PMR occurs in people over 50, which is a very important diagnostic feature; CK and power are normal.

questions.stem: A 79 year old woman with polymyalgia rheumatica stopped her prednisolone a month ago. She has had a left-sided headache and pain in her jaw when eating for a week. This morning she woke with painless, near-total loss of vision in her left eye. Her ESR is 96 mm/hr.

steps.x: **B. Anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy.** GCA visual loss = anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, often irreversible.

questions.stem: A 76 year old woman has had polymyalgia rheumatica for 3 years and has needed prednisolone 5 to 10 mg daily throughout because of relapses. She never started bone protection. A DEXA scan shows a femoral neck T-score of −3.0. Her calcium, PTH and vitamin D are normal.

questions.stem: A 68 year old woman has 2 months of pain and stiffness around both shoulders and thighs. She can barely raise her arms because of pain, yet on formal testing her shoulder abduction and hip flexion power are 5/5. She takes no statins. Investigations:
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.stem: A 71 year old man has 5 weeks of pain in both upper arms and buttocks. He is otherwise well with no headache or visual symptoms. His GP suspects polymyalgia rheumatica and is taking a focused history before checking his blood tests.

questions.stem: An 81 year old man has 4 weeks of pain in both shoulders. He has trouble putting on his coat and cannot reach the top shelf. questions.stem: A 72 year old woman with polymyalgia rheumatica has responded well to prednisolone, which is being tapered. At her review, the GP wants to ask about the symptom that would most suggest she is developing giant cell arteritis.

questions.stem: A 74 year old woman had 6 weeks of bilateral shoulder and hip girdle stiffness and an ESR of 70 mm/hr. Her GP started prednisolone 15 mg daily. Three days later she says she feels '90% better' and can dress herself without help. Her CK was normal.

questions.stem: A 70 year old woman has 7 weeks of aching in both hips and thighs, worse on getting out of bed, with stiffness that lasts over an hour each morning. She also has aches in her wrists and fingers. Hip movement is full but uncomfortable. Her ESR is 66 mm/hr and CRP 52 mg/L.

questions.stem: A 69 year old man has 6 weeks of bilateral shoulder and hip girdle pain with morning stiffness for 2 hours. Power is 5/5, and his ESR is 62 mm/hr and CRP 44 mg/L. A medical student asks how the diagnosis of polymyalgia rheumatica is confirmed.

questions.stem: A 71 year old woman with polymyalgia rheumatica started prednisolone 15 mg daily 4 weeks ago. Her stiffness resolved within a week and her ESR has fallen from 68 to 14 mm/hr. She has no headache or visual symptoms. She is taking calcium and vitamin D.

questions.stem: A 76 year old woman with polymyalgia rheumatica phones her GP surgery. For 3 days she has had a new left-sided headache with scalp tenderness and pain in her jaw on chewing. Her vision is normal. The nearest temporal artery biopsy slot is in 5 days.

questions.stem: A 74 year old woman has been on prednisolone for polymyalgia rheumatica for 2 years at doses of 5 to 10 mg daily and has lost bone density on serial DEXA scans.
